skill.name: wechat-mp-article-extract
skill.description: Use SocialDataX to retrieve WeChat public account articles from a link or pasted share text. Summarize the available text, answer questions, or format it as Markdown.
skill.summary: Retrieve WeChat article text through SocialDataX for summaries, questions, and Markdown archives.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: The skill directs users and agents to run a mutable npm package that can access SocialDataX credentials, including a key stored in plaintext. It sends article input to SocialDataX without requiring prior disclosure of that transfer or possible charges. No evidence of embedded secrets, obfuscation, deliberate credential exfiltration, or prompt injection was found in the skill source.

remediation.issue: Authentication and article retrieval run an unpinned npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin and review an exact release, verify its integrity and dependencies, and run it with minimal filesystem and environment access.

remediation.issue: Login persists a plaintext API key, and the CLI prefers inherited credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Use the operating system credential store or a scoped secret injection mechanism. Avoid passing unrelated environment variables to the CLI.

remediation.issue: Article retrieval can send share text to a third party and consume service credits.
remediation.suggestion: Extract and validate only the WeChat article URL locally. Disclose the destination and possible charges, and require consent before the first retrieval.

remediation.issue: Billing guidance prioritizes a URL from an error response.
remediation.suggestion: Use the documented billing URL or validate the returned URL against an explicit HTTPS origin and path allowlist.

content.value_statement: Standard web readers may show a WeChat article link without its body text. This skill uses SocialDataX to retrieve available text for summaries, questions, or Markdown archives.
actual_capabilities: Request article text from a WeChat public account URL or share text containing one.
Summarize the available text and include the article title and original link when returned.
Answer questions using the retrieved text and distinguish author claims from direct evidence.
Format available article text as Markdown, preserving recognizable paragraphs, lists, and code blocks.
Include returned image links when requested and flag missing or truncated text.
limitations: Retrieval requires command execution, Node.js and npm, network access, and a SocialDataX API key. Requests may consume service credits.
Deleted, restricted, or verification-gated articles may return no readable text.
The CLI does not paginate the article body. Image links alone do not provide the text inside images.
The skill does not discover articles, collect comments or engagement data, or process WeChat Channels videos.

use_cases.title: Brief a Team on an Article
use_cases.description: Summarize the article's main points and include its original link so teammates can review the source.

use_cases.title: Review Evidence in a Source
use_cases.description: Identify the evidence for a specific claim and note which questions the available text cannot answer.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Markdown Archive
use_cases.description: Organize the retrieved body, publication details, and requested image links for a reference collection.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize an Article
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize this WeChat article in three points: [article URL]. Include the title and original link if available.
prompt_templates.scenario: Get a short overview of one linked article.

prompt_templates.title: Ask About a Specific Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this WeChat article: [article URL]. What does the author say about [topic]? Include one short supporting quote if available.
prompt_templates.scenario: Answer a focused question using the article text.

prompt_templates.title: Archive the Available Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Format the available body of this WeChat article as Markdown: [article URL]. Preserve headings and lists. Include returned image links and identify missing sections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare source material for a reference collection.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an Article's Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WeChat article: [article URL]. Separate the author's claims from the evidence given. State which conclusions cannot be assessed from the retrieved text.
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess the evidence without overstating how much of the article was retrieved.

output_examples.input: What evidence does this WeChat article give for extending library hours?
output: The author says evening hours could help commuters use the library.
The article cites an increase in visits during a pilot. It does not report whether those visits came from commuters.
Source: A Trial of Longer Library Hours. The original link accompanies the answer when returned.

output_examples.input: Summarize this article and tell me how the trial ended.
output_examples.output: Only the opening section was retrieved. It describes the trial's purpose, but the available text does not reveal the outcome.

best_practices: Submit only the article URL when possible, and check that you can share it with SocialDataX.
Keep the API key out of chats and logs. Use a reviewed CLI release and enter credentials only through trusted local setup.
Check whether the body is complete before quoting it or archiving it.
anti_patterns: Treating a title, preview, or excerpt as the full article.
Assuming an image link includes a transcription of the text in the image.
Repeating a billable request after an access restriction, incomplete result, or balance error.

faq.question: What inputs can I provide?
faq.answer: Use an article URL on mp.weixin.qq.com or share text containing that URL. A direct URL avoids sending unnecessary share text.

faq.question: Do I need a SocialDataX API key?
faq.answer: Yes, for CLI retrieval. The CLI checks its environment and local configuration. Do not paste the key into chat.

faq.question: Can article retrieval consume credits?
faq.answer: Yes. Article retrieval may consume SocialDataX credits. The documented credential status check does not call the paid article endpoint.

faq.question: Does it log in to my WeChat account?
faq.answer: The documented workflow uses SocialDataX credentials, not a WeChat login. It does not post, like, comment, or change account settings.

faq.question: Can it read text inside article images?
faq.answer: The CLI can return image links, not transcriptions. An assistant with image support may analyze readable screenshots you provide.

faq.question: What happens if the article body is unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill reports the missing text instead of guessing. You can provide the article text for analysis without using the retrieval CLI.
